findings.description: Control first on the same config. `startup` pops the pooled fd and treats `recv(MSG_PEEK|MSG_DONTWAIT)` returning EAGAIN as reusable (`:87`); `delup` returns the fd whenever the head was HTTP/1.1 without `Connection: close` (`:89`, `:71`). A peer that holds one response back and flushes it after the peek hands the victim the attacker's frame byte for byte, 10/10 from cold servers, exec output included. Separate defect on `:86`: `upfail` retries only GET/HEAD, so a dead pooled socket is fatal to a POST — 20/20 POST 502 while GET is retried away when a second upstream exists.
findings.title: Pool liveness is a one-byte check-then-use with no epoch, so a frame the upstream writes after the peek is served to the next client as its own response

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
